request: Add offline substring search to this Python catalog using the application's src/database.py connection. Search must be accent insensitive and Unicode casefold insensitive, without changing displayed titles: cafe finds Café Racer, STRASSE finds Die Straße, and interior query afe finds Café Racer. Query xyz finds no records. An empty query returns no matches. Search order is stable by ID and duplicate titles preserve distinct IDs. The fixed initial catalog fits in memory (at most 5000 titles), search needs no external service, no fuzzy ranking and no new dependency. A previous design note suggests SQLite FTS5 trigram or LIKE if they meet these semantics on this binding; that is a proposal, not an accepted requirement. Verify the chosen mechanism at its real boundary when needed, and retain implementation and consumer checks as future work. Temporary local experiments on disposable data are authorized. Existing tests must remain passing.

# Supplied discovery

This is a constructed planning fixture. Source, tests and data are present; the baseline suite passed. Only existing behavior was tested. No new feature, atomicity or search acceptance is implied. No earlier decision experiment is supplied.

# Architecture

## Stack

Python standard library, sqlite3 connection supplied by src/database.py, unicodedata for search keys. No external service, dependency, fuzzy ranking or SQLite extension required.

## Structure

Existing src/database.py only creates connections; tests/test_baseline.py tests SELECT 1. data/catalog.json contains IDs 1 and 3 with Café Racer and ID 2 with Die Straße. No table creation, data loader, command, UI or search consumer currently exists.

Planned src/search.py owns search(connection, query) -> list of (id, original_title) tuples. Caller supplies application-created connection with catalog(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL) populated. Tests and documented consumer explicitly set up that table from JSON; no implicit startup write or persistent migration is inferred. Existing database.connect(path=':memory:') stays compatible. API is the minimal consumer surface because no CLI/UI was requested.

Namespace/data map (AD-4): only local Python runtime. src is the existing regular package (src/__init__.py); src.database.connect remains the connection seam. New src.search.search is the single public callable, with _search_key private; imports only unicodedata. Tests import through src, with no top-level search.py or stdlib-shadowing modules. New tests/test_search.py is discovered by existing unittest. README gains an executable caller example; no new executable command namespace. Existing paths were inventoried and neither search module nor consumer currently exists.

Storage map (AD-5): data/catalog.json is the supplied immutable seed. Disposable caller/test catalog table has id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and title TEXT NOT NULL, duplicate titles allowed, no relations or secondary index. Each invocation reads original DB rows; normalized keys live only for that call. Caller owns schema, inserts, transactions and cleanup; search performs no DDL/DML. No persisted normalized copy, schema version/migration, background job, retained personal data or externally applied state is needed. Test data lifetime ends with connection close; persistent import and retention policies are outside this additive reader contract.

## Conventions

Observed at seed e39e203: small snake_case functions and direct standard-library imports in src/database.py; unittest.TestCase/assertEqual in tests/test_baseline.py. No formatter, linter, package manifest or type configuration supplied. Naming/layout inferred from those two small exemplars; established error/logging conventions unknown. New code should follow these local patterns and explicitly document connection ownership.

## Interfaces and boundaries

Planned private key(value): value.casefold(), NFD normalize, remove characters with Unicode category Mn; apply identically to titles and query. This covers canonical decomposed accents and Unicode casefold, without compatibility transliteration (e.g. ø is not redefined as o). Preserve raw stored title and ID. Return [] when original or normalized query is empty, before substring matching. Do not strip spaces. Search loads SELECT id, title FROM catalog ORDER BY id on each call and scans in that order; no cache invalidation or stale snapshot contract, title-only deduplication or mutation. O(total title characters) work and memory per query for the bounded catalog. No latency budget is specified.

Caller owns connection, table setup, transactions and close. Search is read-only, must not commit, close, catch database errors as an empty list, or rewrite stored titles. Data scope is integer IDs and non-null string titles as supplied; invalid schemas are errors. No remote cache/authorization/event/outage contract is introduced.

## Real-boundary checks

RB-1 PLANNED: test_TC_01..test_TC_08 in tests/test_search.py run locally with actual src.database.connect and disposable SQLite catalog. Independent literal expected IDs/titles, reverse insertion and Unicode variants verify the Python/SQLite boundary; before/after reads preserve source rows and caller transaction state. Owner search work item, due test. Probe feasibility observed against the same connection, but public implementation and durable tests do not exist.

RB-2 PLANNED consumer procedure (test_TC_09, ConsumerTests): actor Python caller at repository root; initial state no database/table. (1) Open database.connect(). (2) Create in-memory catalog(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL). (3) json.load data/catalog.json and insert parameterized id/title tuples. Explicit fixture setup is authorized and required because the application currently has no loader. (4) Import src.search.search and call with this connection and cafe, STRASSE, afe, xyz, then empty. (5) Observe exact ordered tuples: [(1,'Café Racer'),(3,'Café Racer')], [(2,'Die Straße')], first tuple list again, [], []. (6) Verify original ordered rows unchanged and connection usable; close in finally. Owner search work item, due test and system-test/product-acceptance. This procedure is NOT-REPLAYED against product: src.search is absent. The disposable probe walked setup/read/scan on the supplied binding and independently asserted these literal outcomes; it did not perform step 4's product import. README caller example must match this setup and be replayed later. No browser needed for the Python API surface.

No authorized remote endpoint or external credential is supplied; remote permissions, deployment or hosted-consumer claims cannot be observed and are not claimed. Offline requirements need only this local runtime. Persistent target state: none for in-memory fixtures. Base tests get fresh fixtures; base API absence must cause retained assertions to fail, never reuse candidate state.

## Decisions

AD-1: Preserve standard-library stack and baseline; accepted.

AD-2: Choose Python normalized substring scan over rows fetched using the real application SQLite connection, on each call. Authorized disposable boundary experiment observed all required examples and 5000 rows, preserving displayed titles and IDs. The fixed memory bound permits this simple mechanism. Original-title LIKE demonstrably failed cafe; FTS5/trigram was a proposal, not an obligation, and introduces unnecessary extension/tokenization uncertainty. No claim about untested FTS5 capabilities. This chooses a feasible design, not a passing implementation.

AD-3: Provide search(connection, query) as public API and document a local caller with explicit fixture/table setup. This is a planning assumption, since the supplied catalog has no existing consumer or schema. A future persistent import/startup workflow would require separate scope; no invented CLI, migration or deployment is required for the request.

AD-4: Plan responsibility/namespace placement in src.search, beside existing src.database; private _search_key, public search(connection, query), tests/test_search.py and README caller. Status selected for implementation. Preserves package imports and avoids generic top-level or stdlib-shadowing names; no other execution runtime. Revalidate on added caller or namespace collision.

AD-5: Plan a read-only reader over caller-owned catalog(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL), with JSON only seeding disposable consumer fixtures. Status selected assumption, to confirm at W1 step-plan. Explicit setup is necessary because no application table/loader exists. No persistent schema migration is authorized or needed; every caller owns its connection and receives untouched titles.

AD-6: Plan synchronous in-process caller -> search -> SQLite SELECT -> ordered tuples. Status selected. No acknowledgment transfers durable work, no push/poll, cross-user state or shared cache. Errors propagate to the caller; source and pending transaction remain intact. Local consumer test_TC_09 and ownership/error test_TC_08 must prove the contract after implementation; a crash creates no accepted background task and search has no mutation to recover.

## Superseded

The earlier undecided publication/command responsibility and provisional FTS/LIKE suggestion are resolved by AD-2 and AD-3; no previously accepted feature is removed.

# Environment

## Targets and runtimes

Local Python standard library only. Observed Python 3.9.6, sqlite3 SQLite 3.54.0 and Unicode 13.0.0. The target is the supplied application connection in src/database.py. Disposable in-memory SQLite databases isolate each test; explicitly close connections (the SQLite connection context manager alone does not close them). No external target, account, endpoint or credential is supplied or authorized. No network or dependency installation is required.

## Commands

Run from the repository root. Existing full suite and current ID listing, inclusion: every discovered test_*.py under tests; expected cost under a second at present:
```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```
Observed exit 0, exactly test_application_connection, one test. It does not yet include search coverage. After authoring, this same command must discover all test_TC_01 through test_TC_09 plus the baseline. A zero-selected run is failure, never acceptance.

Existing smoke, same fixture-free connection check, bounded to one case:
```sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_baseline.Baseline.test_application_connection -v
```
Observed exit 0, one baseline case. This smoke says nothing about search.

Focused feature route, PLANNED; after tests/test_search.py is authored, inclusion: all nine search and consumer IDs below, expected cost seconds including 5000 titles:
```sh
python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_search -v
```
Readiness attempt exited 1: ModuleNotFoundError for tests.test_search. That is an authoring prerequisite for test-spec, not a feature RED result. Do not claim focused success until cases exist, execute and print their IDs. No dependency setup is missing.

## Skills

Execution uses the selected ShipLoop and bound Improve skills. No product-specific skill or external integration is needed.

## Harnesses and suites

Definition: existing tests/test_baseline.py, unittest.TestCase, stdlib runner via Commands. Available now; direct observed assertions prove application connection executes SELECT 1. No coverage package or configured coverage threshold exists; use explicit clause-to-case assertions and suite discovery rather than inventing a coverage percentage. Revalidate after interpreter, source, schema or test registration changes.

Planned facility: tests/test_search.py with SearchTests and ConsumerTests, unittest, one fresh database.connect() per case with catalog(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL); populate disposable fixture and close in cleanup. Use supplied JSON for the consumer case. Author owns setup/teardown at test-spec, and validates registration before test. tests are missing, runner is available. No new framework is needed. No shared mutable fixtures or persistent target state.

All cases below are PLANNED and due after implementation at test; consumer additionally reruns at system-test/product-acceptance. Owner: the search work item. Required surfaces are Python API on a real application-created SQLite connection and the documented caller. ## Platform facts

A disposable experiment through src.database.connect read and searched real SQLite rows using Python casefold, NFD normalization and removal of Unicode Mn marks. Required examples, decomposed accents, original titles, stable distinct IDs, and 5000-row workload succeeded. Raw SQLite LIKE on %cafe% returned [] for Café Racer, contradicting that proposed mechanism. FTS5/trigram is not selected or required; its availability and tokenization are unverified. # Product specification

## Requirements
